name: Soundgarden
label: Sub Pop
lede: Named after a sculpture that moans in the wind, they gave Sub Pop its reason to exist, became the first grunge band on a major label, and are still finishing the last songs Chris Cornell sang on.

eras.title: A singing drummer and a sculpture on the lake
eras.text: Two friends from Park Forest, Illinois, Kim Thayil and Hiro Yamamoto, found a Seattle drummer who could really sing. Within two years Soundgarden had a proper drummer, a manager and three songs on the compilation that first put a name to the Seattle sound.

years.h: Chris Cornell, Kim Thayil and Hiro Yamamoto start Soundgarden
years.p: [[Chris Cornell|cbf9738d-8f81-4a92-bc64-ede09341652d]] sings from behind the drum kit; Hiro Yamamoto plays bass and Kim Thayil guitar. Cornell and Yamamoto had played together in a covers band called the Shemps.

years.h: The name comes from A Sound Garden, a sculpture that hums
years.p: A Sound Garden is a 1983 sculpture of pipes on the NOAA grounds by Magnuson Park that make eerie tones when the wind blows through them.

years.h: Scott Sundquist on drums; Chris Cornell steps out front
years.p: Drummer [[Scott Sundquist|2a1cc59e-5465-417c-af9e-115a432e614b]] joins so Chris Cornell can sing standing up.

years.cap: Soundgarden at the Paramount Theatre, Seattle, 2013 · Wikimedia
q: That was one of the best shows I've seen in my whole life.
years.h: The Rainbow Tavern show that gets Sub Pop started
years.p: Jonathan Poneman, booking the Rainbow Tavern near the University of Washington, sees a bare-chested Chris Cornell and decides to put money behind the band.
years.xp: Poneman teamed with [[Bruce Pavitt|f5230572-06e4-453c-a1dd-7a4b560da3bb]], who had known Kim Thayil back in the Midwest and was running Sub Pop as a fanzine and cassette series without money to press records. Poneman put in $20,000, and Sub Pop became a label.

years.h: Matt Cameron replaces Scott Sundquist; Susan Silver manages
years.p: [[Matt Cameron|07e93890-46a1-4ebd-9a70-3988a2135d87]], drummer for [[Skin Yard|0119843b-4d56-47b6-ac0d-11528259bf0a]], takes over from Scott Sundquist, who leaves to spend time with his family. [[Susan Silver|bdd26cdc-cbc9-4def-8d74-d15e871e5129]] becomes Soundgarden's manager.

years.h: Three songs on Deep Six, the C/Z grunge sampler
years.p: Soundgarden share C/Z Records' Deep Six with [[Green River|78f56916-fe11-4110-8f10-d553ddf8de7b]], the [[Melvins|9ccfbc94-a4f4-42f7-b6f5-d903ab77cccb]], [[Malfunkshun|71f4a8ff-97ba-47c6-a729-7f87de77c796]], [[Skin Yard|0119843b-4d56-47b6-ac0d-11528259bf0a]] and the U-Men.

eras.title: Sub Pop's first big bet
eras.text: Soundgarden's first records came out on the label they had inspired, with Jack Endino behind the board. Then they went to Greg Ginn's SST for an album, and signed with A&M before it was even out.

years.h: Hunted Down: Soundgarden's first Sub Pop single
years.p: Hunted Down backed with Nothing to Say is Soundgarden's first single, one of the first records on Sub Pop as a label.

years.h: Screaming Life EP, produced by Jack Endino
years.p: Six songs recorded with Jack Endino at Reciprocal Recording, the Seattle studio that would soon make Bleach for [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]].

years.h: Fopp EP: an Ohio Players cover as a calling card
years.p: Soundgarden's second Sub Pop EP leads with a cover of the Ohio Players' Fopp, recorded with Steve Fisk.

years.h: Soundgarden become the first grunge band signed to a major
years.p: Soundgarden sign with A&M Records, per Wikipedia the first band of the Seattle scene on a major label.

years.h: Ultramega OK on SST, and a Grammy nomination
years.p: The debut album comes out on [[Greg Ginn|4f35de64-27ab-4426-95fd-8d454cda4e48]]'s SST. It is nominated for the first-ever Best Metal Performance Grammy in 1990, which goes to [[Metallica|65f4f0c5-ef9e-490c-aee3-909e7ae6b2ab]].

eras.title: Frowngarden
eras.text: On A&M the band got louder, lost two bassists in a year, and found Ben Shepherd. Then came the wrong tour with Guns N' Roses, a tribute record for a dead friend, and Badmotorfinger.

years.h: Louder Than Love: the first grunge album on the Billboard 200
years.p: Soundgarden's A&M debut peaks at No. 108, the first grunge record to reach the chart, according to Wikipedia.

years.h: Hiro Yamamoto quits; Jason Everman arrives from Nirvana
years.p: Hiro Yamamoto, frustrated at his shrinking role, leaves and goes back to college. [[Jason Everman|797dc323-fc39-4597-98cc-d10493f67326]], months out of [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]], takes over on bass.

years.h: Mother Love Bone's Andrew Wood dies of a heroin overdose
years.p: [[Andrew Wood|400e187f-31b0-473d-a4c3-685d38229274]], singer of [[Mother Love Bone|a5585acd-9b65-49a7-a63b-3cc4ee18846e]] and Chris Cornell's former roommate, dies at 24. Cornell writes songs for him that become Temple of the Dog.

years.h: Jason Everman fired; Ben Shepherd joins on bass
years.p: Jason Everman is fired after the Louder Than Love tour. [[Ben Shepherd|0bd73a25-9156-4c0a-aa17-90d06b9275ad]], who had once nearly played guitar in [[Nirvana|5b11f4ce-a62d-471e-81fc-a69a8278c7da]], takes the bass job.
years.xp: Everman later called the firing heartbreaking, and eventually joined the U.S. Army. Shepherd had befriended Kurt Cobain at an Olympia party; he said he was meant to play lead guitar for Nirvana, but they stayed a trio.

years.h: Temple of the Dog: Chris Cornell's tribute to Andrew Wood
years.p: With Stone Gossard, Jeff Ament and Mike McCready of the band that became [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]]. A new singer, [[Eddie Vedder|1a60d6dd-9d3e-40fc-a66d-3184f9ee0d61]], duets with Chris Cornell on Hunger Strike.

years.h: Badmotorfinger: odd time signatures, No. 39, double platinum
years.p: Soundgarden's heaviest record breaks them into the mainstream. MTV bans the Jesus Christ Pose video, and the band gets death threats on tour in the U.K., per Wikipedia.

years.h: Opening for Guns N' Roses on the Use Your Illusion tour
years.p: Soundgarden open arenas for [[Guns N' Roses|eeb1195b-f213-4ce1-b28c-8565211f8e43]]. GN'R's crew nicknamed them Frowngarden for staying out of the excess.
years.xp: When manager Susan Silver announced the offer, the band sat silent for about thirty seconds. Matt Cameron said later that Axl Rose made the band wait an hour or two to go on; Ben Shepherd said he had no use for rock stars.

years.h: Lollapalooza, and a cameo in Cameron Crowe's Singles
years.p: Soundgarden play the main stage of Lollapalooza 1992 and perform Birth Ritual in Cameron Crowe's Seattle film Singles.

eras.title: A number one record and a bass in the air
eras.text: Superunknown made Soundgarden one of the biggest rock bands in the world. Two years later the band was arguing over how heavy to be, and a bass guitar thrown in Honolulu ended it.

years.h: Superunknown debuts at No. 1
years.p: Soundgarden's fourth album enters the Billboard 200 at the top and goes six times platinum, their biggest record by far.
years.xp: Spoonman features [[Artis the Spoonman|c75a51e1-2c04-4663-a664-bafe0aebf23d]], a Seattle street performer, playing spoons. Black Hole Sun became the album's signature, its video winning an MTV award and later a Clio.

years.h: Two Grammys: Spoonman and Black Hole Sun
years.p: Spoonman wins Best Metal Performance and Black Hole Sun wins Best Hard Rock Performance at the 1995 Grammys.

years.h: Down on the Upside: mandolins and arguments
years.p: A looser, stranger record, made amid friction over how far to move from heavy riffs. It debuts at No. 2 and Soundgarden headline Lollapalooza with [[Metallica|65f4f0c5-ef9e-490c-aee3-909e7ae6b2ab]].

years.cap: Chris Cornell and Kim Thayil, 2013 · Wikimedia
years.h: Last show in Honolulu: Ben Shepherd throws his bass and walks
years.p: When his gear failed, Ben Shepherd threw his bass into the air and stormed off. Chris Cornell came back alone for the encore.

years.h: Soundgarden announce their breakup
years.p: The band splits after thirteen years. Kim Thayil says dissatisfaction had been obvious for half a year. The hits collection A-Sides follows that November.
years.xp: Matt Cameron joined [[Pearl Jam|83b9cbe7-9857-49e2-ab8e-b57b01038103]] in 1998. Chris Cornell made solo records and fronted [[Audioslave|020bfbb4-05c3-4c86-b372-17825c262094]] with members of [[Rage Against the Machine|3798b104-01cb-484c-a3b0-56adc6399b80]] from 2001 to 2007.

eras.title: School is back in session
eras.text: Thirteen years after the split, Soundgarden came back on a tweet. They toured the world again and made one more album before Chris Cornell's death in Detroit.

q: The 12-year break is over and school is back in session.
years.h: Chris Cornell announces the reunion on Twitter
years.p: On New Year's Day Chris Cornell tells fans Soundgarden are back.

years.h: First show in 13 years, billed as Nudedragons
years.p: Soundgarden play the Showbox at the Market in Seattle under an anagram of their name, then headline Lollapalooza in Chicago that August.

years.h: King Animal: the first new album in 16 years
years.p: Soundgarden's sixth album, and the last one released in Chris Cornell's lifetime.

years.h: Chris Cornell dies in Detroit after a Fox Theatre show, age 52
years.p: Hours after playing the Fox Theatre, Chris Cornell was found in his room at the MGM Grand Detroit. The Wayne County medical examiner ruled it suicide by hanging.

eras.title: The last songs, fought over and finished
eras.text: Without Chris Cornell the band said it was done, then spent years in court with his widow over seven songs he'd sung on. Settlement brought the survivors back together, a Hall of Fame night with their original bassist, and a final album in progress.

years.h: Kim Thayil: there were four of us, now there's three
years.p: Kim Thayil tells the Seattle Times Soundgarden has little left to do beyond catalog work.

years.h: I Am the Highway: the tribute at the Forum
years.p: Kim Thayil, Matt Cameron and Ben Shepherd play eight songs with guest singers including [[Taylor Momsen|d1ecf86c-3d89-420e-b8c1-bceb6b101c61]] and [[Brandi Carlile|baf05baf-69fb-47dd-93c2-033536b8c385]] at the Forum in Inglewood.

years.h: Soundgarden and Vicky Cornell settle their lawsuits
years.p: Chris Cornell's widow sued in 2019 over seven unreleased songs he sang on, and the band countersued. The out-of-court resolution clears the way for the band to finish the songs.
years.xp: Vicky Cornell claimed the band withheld royalties to force her hand on the seven songs. The band's countersuit was over the money from the 2019 tribute concert and the social media accounts.

years.h: Nudedragons again: a benefit for Seattle Children's
years.p: The surviving members play their first show since the 2019 tribute, under the same anagram they used in 2010.

years.h: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, with Hiro Yamamoto back on bass
years.p: Kim Thayil, Matt Cameron and Ben Shepherd play the induction with original bassist Hiro Yamamoto, his first time onstage with them in 36 years, and singers including Taylor Momsen and [[Jerry Cantrell|960eb93f-e73c-4df8-864d-08a06c2dcc11]].

years.h: The final Soundgarden album is past halfway
years.p: The survivors say they are more than halfway through the eight songs recorded with Chris Cornell, aimed at 2027, ten years after his death.
